unit.title: Coordinate the installation of substation plant and apparatus

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main job of a distribution substation that supplies a hotel or a factory?
options: To store electricity in batteries for use during power cuts
To generate electricity for the building from diesel fuel
To step the power company's medium voltage down to low voltage
To change the frequency of the supply to suit the machines

questions.stem: Who may enter a live substation and operate its switchgear?
options: Only persons authorised under the safety rules
Any electrician who holds a Level 3 certificate
Trainees, as long as the instructor waits at the gate
The site foreman of the building contractor

questions.stem: In a substation, what is the job of a surge arrester?
options: It measures the energy used for the monthly bill
It sends lightning and switching surges to earth
It cools the transformer oil in hot weather
It stops the transformer from being overloaded

questions.stem: What is a ring main unit (RMU)?
options: A low-voltage board that feeds the ring circuits for sockets in a building
A metal ring fitted round the transformer to carry earth fault current
A meter that records how often the supply ring is interrupted
Compact MV switchgear that switches the ring cables and feeds the transformer

questions.stem: Why are current transformers (CTs) fitted in a substation?
options: To raise the supply voltage for large motors
To store current for use after the breaker trips
To feed relays and meters a small, matching current
To share the building's load between two transformers

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an earth switch on medium-voltage switchgear?
options: To earth isolated conductors so they are safe to work on
To switch the building's outdoor lighting off at night
To test the resistance of the earth electrodes automatically
To start the standby generator when the supply fails

questions.stem: A transformer must go inside a hotel building, close to guest rooms. Why might the specification ask for a dry-type transformer instead of an oil-filled one?
options: It is always cheaper and lighter than an oil type
It needs no ventilation or cooling of any kind in use
It can safely be worked on while it is energised
It has no oil, so the fire and spill risk is lower

questions.stem: Why does an oil-filled transformer stand inside a bund (a low wall or pit) at many sites?
options: To stop rainwater from cooling the transformer tank too quickly
To hold any oil that leaks so it does not spread or pollute
To raise the transformer up for easier lifting later
To keep members of the public from seeing the tank

questions.stem: A transformer is rated 12 000 V / 240 V. What is its voltage ratio?
A three-phase transformer is rated 500 kVA with a 480 V secondary. Using I = kVA × 1000 ÷ (1.732 × V), what is its full-load secondary current?
options: About 1 042 A
About 347 A
About 1 804 A
About 601 A

questions.stem: A factory's maximum demand is 380 kW at a power factor of 0.8. Which is the smallest of these standard transformer sizes that can carry it?
options: 300 kVA
400 kVA
500 kVA
750 kVA

questions.stem: Which drawing shows the main electrical connections of a substation, using one line for each three-phase circuit?
options: The single-line diagram
The civil foundation drawing
The site location map
The cable schedule

questions.stem: The layout drawing and the transformer maker's drawing show different positions for the cable entries. What should the coordinator do?
options: Let the civil contractor choose whichever one is easier to build
Follow the layout drawing, since it was issued first
Leave out the cable ducts and core-drill them later
Raise a query with the designer and get a written reply first

questions.stem: Where would you find the transformer's required kVA, voltages, vector group and cooling type for a project?
options: On the power company's monthly bill
In the project specification and equipment schedule
In the building's fire safety plan
In the crane hire company's quotation

questions.stem: Why is the power company involved early when a customer substation is being planned?
options: It must pay for the customer's transformer and switchgear
It chooses which electrical contractor will do the work
It sets the supply point, its own equipment and the rules
It decides the paint colour of the substation building

questions.stem: Which job usually must be finished before the transformer is delivered to site?
options: The plinth, cured and ready, with the cable ducts in place
The final commissioning tests on all the protection relays
The handover of the operation and maintenance manuals
Energising the low-voltage main switchboard

questions.stem: On the Gantt chart for the substation project, what does the critical path show?
options: The tasks that are the most dangerous to do
The route the crane takes across the site
The tasks that will cost the most money
The chain of tasks where any delay delays the whole job

questions.stem: The switchgear will arrive two weeks late, but the cable crew is booked for next week. What is the best action?
options: Keep the cable crew on site doing nothing until it arrives
Re-plan the work and tell everyone affected
Fit any other switchgear that is in stock instead
Tell nobody and hope the delivery comes early

questions.stem: A new transformer arrives on a truck. Which check is done before it is unloaded and signed for?
options: Count the bolts on the lid and paint over any scratches found
Fill it with extra oil right up to the top of the tank
Look for damage and leaks, and match the nameplate to the order
Energise it on the truck to prove that it works

questions.stem: Why is a written lifting plan needed to place a transformer on its plinth?
options: The crane, slings and exclusion zone must suit the load
The insurer needs to know the colour and make of the crane used
It lets the crane driver work without a signaller
It means the transformer can be lifted by its bushings

questions.stem: When a transformer is lifted, where should the slings be attached?
options: Round the bushings, as they are the highest point
Round the cooling fins to spread the load
To the cable boxes on each side
Only to the lifting lugs the maker provides

questions.stem: Switchgear arrives a month before it can be installed. How should it be stored?
options: Outside in the sun with the covers off, so moisture dries out
On the bare ground beside the cable trench
Dry, covered and off the ground, as the maker says
Unpacked, so it is ready to fit straight away

questions.stem: Why does a substation have an earth grid (earth mat) buried under and around it?
options: To stop termites from damaging the buried cables
To keep step and touch voltages safe during an earth fault
To carry the neutral current all the way back to the power station
To make the concrete plinth stronger

questions.stem: What is meant by 'touch voltage' at a substation?
options: The voltage between metalwork a person touches and the ground
The voltage a person feels when touching a battery
The voltage shown on a tester when its probes touch
The supply voltage at the socket outlet nearest to the substation

questions.stem: Why are the substation fence and gate bonded to the earth system?
options: So the gate lock does not rust in the sea air
So the fence acts as the lightning conductor for the building
So a fault cannot leave a dangerous voltage on the fence
So that anyone climbing the fence gets a warning shock

questions.stem: Why must medium-voltage (MV) cable terminations be made by a trained jointer, following the kit maker's instructions exactly?
options: The kits are expensive and must not be wasted
Only jointers are allowed to use a cable knife
The colour of the kit must match the cable sheath
Small errors in cutting back or cleaning can cause a failure

questions.stem: Before a new MV cable is connected, which test shows whether its insulation is sound?
options: A continuity buzzer test from one end only
An insulation test by the competent testing team
Looking along the outer sheath for scratches
Switching it on to see whether or not the breaker trips

questions.stem: What does an overcurrent and earth fault relay do in a substation?
options: It senses a fault through the CTs and trips the breaker
It counts the energy used for the monthly bill
It raises the voltage when the load is heavy
It starts the cooling fans when the oil is cold

questions.stem: Why does a substation with circuit breakers have its own battery and charger?
options: To run all of the building's lights during a power cut
To start the standby generator once a week
So breakers can still trip if the AC supply is lost
To keep the transformer oil warm at night

questions.stem: A Buchholz relay is fitted on many oil-filled transformers that have a conservator tank. What does it detect?
options: The outside air temperature around the tank
Gas or a sudden oil surge from a fault inside
Rainwater collecting in the low-voltage cable box
The total kWh used by the building's load

questions.stem: What is the main difference between an isolator (disconnector) and a circuit breaker?
options: An isolator can interrupt fault current; a breaker cannot
They are the same; the names change by country
An isolator is for DC only; a breaker is for AC only
A breaker can interrupt fault current; an isolator cannot

questions.stem: Many modern MV switches use SF6 gas. Why must SF6 be handled only by trained people with the right equipment?
options: It harms the climate, and used gas can hold toxic by-products
It is highly flammable and explodes in strong sunlight
It is the same as cooking gas and has a very strong smell
It makes the switch live even when it is open

questions.stem: Why can a de-energised MV cable still be dangerous before it has been earthed?
options: It may be too heavy to move safely
Its outer sheath may still be very hot from the sun
It can hold a charge or pick up induced voltage
Its warning labels may have faded

questions.stem: Safety rules for MV switchgear panels warn of 'arc flash'. What does this term mean?
options: The light of a welding arc seen from far away
The bright flash of the meter display when the power returns
A camera flash used when taking site photos
A blast of heat and light from a fault, able to burn

questions.stem: Your crew must dig a cable trench close to an existing live substation. What is the right control?
options: Dig quickly by machine so the time near live plant is short
Work under a permit, with live cables located and marked first
Ask the trainees to watch for sparks while the digger works
Switch off the substation yourself so the area is safe

questions.stem: In this unit, what part do trainees play in substation work?
options: Planning, drawings and checks away from live plant only
They operate the switchgear under the instructor's eye
They earth the MV cables before the jointer starts
They energise the transformer for the first time

questions.stem: Which document allows the jointer to start work on an MV cable that has been isolated and earthed?
options: A delivery note from the cable supplier
The building contractor's daily diary
A permit to work from the authorised person
The crane company's lifting certificate

questions.stem: Which test checks that a transformer's windings give the correct voltage ratio?
options: An earth electrode test
A turns ratio test
An oil level check
A contact resistance test

questions.stem: Why is a sample of a new transformer's oil tested before it is energised?
options: To find out how much the oil cost per litre
To check that it is the same colour as the oil in the old unit
To measure how hot the tank will run in full sun
To check moisture has not weakened its insulating strength

questions.stem: Who energises a new customer substation for the first time?
options: Authorised persons, after all tests and approvals
The electrical contractor's newest apprentice
The building owner, as soon as the fence is up
Any member of the installation crew on site

questions.stem: Before the power company connects a new substation, what must usually be in place?
options: A photograph of the whole crew standing next to the transformer
A receipt for the hire of the crane
A certificate of inspection and approval for the installation
The results of the building's fire alarm test

questions.stem: At handover, why are 'as-built' drawings given to the owner?
options: They show the first ideas, before any design was done
They show what was really installed, including changes
They show the prices of each piece of equipment
They show where the crane stood during the lift

questions.stem: During your inspection before energising, you find a cable gland on the LV side that has not been tightened. As coordinator, what do you do?
options: Ignore it, as the LV side is not important
Tighten it yourself and say nothing to anyone
Sign the checklist and leave it for the client
Record it as a defect, have it fixed and recheck it

questions.stem: You coordinate a civil crew, a cable crew and the jointers on one small site. What helps most to avoid clashes?
options: A daily briefing with a shared programme and clear work areas
Letting each crew start whenever they arrive
Speaking only to the crew that complains the most
Putting all the crews in one trench at the same time

questions.stem: Which is the best place for a pad-mounted substation in a hotel car park near the sea?
options: In the lowest corner of the car park, hidden from guests
Under a large tree, to keep it shaded from the sun
Above flood level, with access and clearances kept
Against the pool fence, so the cables are short

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the oil tank mounted above some transformers that lets the oil expand and contract as it heats and cools?
What do the letters VT stand for, for the device that gives meters and relays a small voltage in step with the main voltage?
A three-phase load takes 300 A at 480 V. Using kVA = 1.732 × V × I ÷ 1000, what is the load in kVA, to the nearest whole number?
What is the concrete base called on which a pad-mounted transformer stands?
What two-word term names the voltage between a person's two feet when fault current flows through the ground near a substation?
What type of bar chart is commonly used to show a project's tasks against time?
What two-word term describes how a three-phase transformer's windings are connected and the phase shift between them, for example Dyn11?
A transformer's rating is written in kVA. Write kVA in full words.
A transformer nameplate shows the cooling type ONAN. What do these four letters stand for?
What is the name of the copper or aluminium bars inside switchgear that carry the current to each circuit?
What instrument measures the resistance of the substation's earth electrodes?
At what supply frequency, in hertz, does the power system in Jamaica run?
What is fitted to a transformer during transport to show whether it was dropped or jolted hard on the way?
The specification says the bund must hold 110% of the transformer's oil. The transformer holds 800 litres. What bund capacity, in litres, is needed?
In many ring main units, which protective device in the transformer circuit must be replaced after it has operated?

essays.stem: Name the main items of plant and apparatus in a pad-mounted customer substation and explain the job of each.
essays.modelAnswer: The medium-voltage switchgear, often a ring main unit, receives the power company's cables and switches the supply to the transformer; it usually has switches, an earth switch and fuses or a breaker to protect the transformer. The transformer steps the medium voltage down to the building's low voltage. It may be oil-filled, with a conservator, a Buchholz relay and a bund, or dry type. Surge arresters send lightning and switching surges to earth to protect the transformer and cables. Current and voltage transformers give small, matching signals to the protection relays and meters. The relays sense faults and trip the breaker, often powered by a substation battery and charger so they work even if the AC supply is lost. The metering records energy for billing. The low-voltage main switchboard takes the transformer's output and feeds the building. The earth grid and electrodes keep step and touch voltages safe in a fault. Finally, the fence, gates, locks and danger signs keep unauthorised people out.
markingPoints: MV switchgear or RMU: switches and protects the incoming supply and transformer
Transformer: steps down MV to LV, with its accessories
Protection: CTs, VTs, relays and DC battery supply
Surge arresters and earthing explained
LV switchboard, metering and the fence, locks and signs

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan and programme the installation of a pad-mounted substation at a hotel in Ocho Rios, from approved design to handover.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start with the approved drawings, the specification and the power company's requirements, and list every task and who does it. I would check the lead times for the transformer and switchgear and order them early, as they are often the longest items. The programme would follow this order: site survey and setting out; locating existing services; civil works for the plinth, bund, cable trenches, ducts and fence; installing the earth grid and electrodes; delivery, inspection and lifting of the transformer and switchgear; laying and terminating the MV and LV cables; fitting the protection, metering and LV board; then inspection and testing by the competent testing team, the government inspection and approval, and energising by authorised persons. I would show this on a Gantt chart with the critical path, allowing for curing time for concrete and for weather, such as the hurricane season. I would hold regular coordination meetings, update the programme when things change, and plan the handover documents from the start.
markingPoints: Uses approved drawings, specification and power company rules
Orders long-lead items early
Gives a logical sequence: civil, earthing, delivery, cables, testing, approval, energising
Uses a Gantt chart with the critical path and allows for curing and weather
Holds coordination meetings and updates the programme

essays.stem: Explain how you would coordinate the different parties involved in installing a customer substation, and how you would keep communication clear.
essays.modelAnswer: Many parties are involved: the owner, the designer, the power company, the civil contractor, the crane company, the cable crew, the jointers, the testing team and the government electrical inspector. I would first make a list of who is responsible for each task and each interface, such as who supplies the cable terminations and who connects at the supply point. I would share one programme with everyone and agree dates in advance, especially for deliveries, crane lifts, outages and inspections. I would hold a short daily briefing on site and a weekly coordination meeting, with written minutes and actions. Drawing queries would go to the designer in writing, and changes would be recorded and the drawings updated. I would give each crew a clear work area so that crews do not clash. I would keep the power company and the inspector informed early, as their dates are hard to change. Any problem, such as a late delivery, would be reported at once, with a revised plan.
markingPoints: Identifies the parties involved
Sets clear responsibilities and interfaces
Uses one shared programme with agreed dates
Uses briefings and meetings with written minutes and actions
Handles queries, changes and delays in writing and promptly

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive, inspect and store a new transformer and MV switchgear delivered to site.
essays.modelAnswer: Before delivery, I would check that the access route, the unloading area and the storage space are ready, and that the lifting plan is in place. When the truck arrives, I would check the delivery note against the purchase order and the specification. I would look for damage to the tank, fins, bushings and switchgear panels, for oil leaks and for broken seals, and read the shock indicator if one is fitted. I would match the nameplate to the order: kVA, voltages, vector group, cooling type and serial number. Any damage or mismatch would be photographed, written on the delivery note before signing and reported to the supplier at once. Items would be unloaded only with the planned crane and slings on the maker's lifting points. If they cannot be installed straight away, I would store them as the maker says: dry, covered, off the ground, with packing and covers left on, and the area secured. I would record everything in the receiving log.
markingPoints: Prepares the route, area and lifting plan beforehand
Checks paperwork and nameplate against the order and specification
Inspects for damage, leaks and the shock indicator
Records and reports any problems before signing
Stores items as the maker says and keeps a record

essays.stem: Explain what a lifting plan for placing a transformer on its plinth should cover, and why each part matters.
essays.modelAnswer: The lifting plan starts with the weight of the transformer from the maker's data, and its centre of gravity, because the crane and slings must be chosen for the real load. It names the crane, its position and its safe working load at the needed reach, and checks the ground can take the crane's outriggers, because soft ground can make the crane overturn. It lists the slings and shackles, with their ratings and certificates, and says they attach only to the maker's lifting lugs, so the bushings and fins are not damaged. It names a competent person in charge of the lift and a signaller, so that only one person gives signals. It checks for overhead lines and sets an exclusion zone, so nobody stands under the load. It sets weather limits, such as no lifting in high wind. It also covers how the transformer is lowered and lined up with the cable entries. Everyone involved is briefed on the plan before the lift starts.
markingPoints: Load weight and centre of gravity from maker's data
Crane, position, capacity and ground conditions
Rated slings on the maker's lifting points
Competent person, one signaller, exclusion zone and overhead lines
Weather limits and a briefing before the lift

essays.stem: Explain why a substation needs a good earthing system, what step and touch voltages are, and what you would check during its installation.
essays.modelAnswer: When an earth fault happens at a substation, a large current flows into the ground. The earthing system gives this current an easy path, so the protection operates quickly, and keeps the voltage on metal parts low. Touch voltage is the voltage between a metal part a person is touching, such as the transformer tank or fence, and the ground where they stand. Step voltage is the voltage between a person's two feet as the current spreads through the soil. A buried earth grid, bonded to all metalwork, keeps both at safe levels. During installation I would check that the grid conductors, rods and joints are the size and type in the specification and are laid at the depth and spacing on the drawing, before the trench is backfilled. I would check that every item of metalwork, including the fence, gates and plinth steel, is bonded. I would photograph buried work and make sure the earth resistance is tested and recorded by the testing team against the design figure.
markingPoints: Explains the earth fault current path and fast protection
Defines touch voltage correctly
Defines step voltage correctly
Checks grid size, depth, joints and bonding before backfilling
Ensures earth resistance is tested and recorded against the design

essays.stem: Describe the main hazards when a substation is installed next to existing live plant, the controls for each, and why trainees never enter a live substation.
essays.modelAnswer: The main hazard is high voltage: contact with, or even approach to, live MV conductors can cause electric shock and arc flash, which burns and can kill. Controls are that only authorised persons operate or enter live plant, under the owner's or power company's safety rules, with a permit to work, isolation, locking, earthing and proving. De-energised cables can hold a charge or have induced voltage, so they are earthed by authorised persons before work. Digging can strike live buried cables, so cables are located and marked, and hand digging is used near them. Heavy lifts are controlled by a lifting plan and exclusion zone. Oil spills and SF6 gas are handled by trained people as the maker says. Trenches need support and barriers. Trainees never enter a live substation because they are not authorised, the distances and rules are strict, and one mistake can be fatal. In this unit they learn the planning, drawings and checks away from live plant.
markingPoints: Identifies HV shock and arc flash as the main hazards
Authorised persons, safety rules, permits, isolation and earthing
Controls for induced voltage, buried cables and lifting
Mentions oil, SF6 or trench hazards with controls
Explains why trainees never enter a live substation

essays.stem: A factory's maximum demand is 520 kW at a power factor of 0.85, and the client wants 20% spare for growth. Standard sizes are 500, 750 and 1 000 kVA. Work out the transformer size, and its full-load current at 480 V three-phase (I = kVA × 1000 ÷ (1.732 × V)). Show your working.
essays.modelAnswer: First change the demand from kW to kVA by dividing by the power factor: 520 ÷ 0.85 = 611.8 kVA. Next add 20% for growth: 611.8 × 1.2 = 734.1 kVA. The smallest standard size that is not less than 734.1 kVA is 750 kVA, so I would choose a 750 kVA transformer. A 500 kVA unit would be overloaded even now, and 1 000 kVA would cost more and run lightly loaded, with higher losses for the load it carries. The full-load secondary current is I = 750 × 1000 ÷ (1.732 × 480) = 750 000 ÷ 831.4 = about 902 A. This current is used to choose the LV main breaker, the busbars and the size and number of LV cables. I would check the result with the designer and the specification, as the final choice may also depend on the power company's rules, the motor starting loads and the space available.
markingPoints: Converts kW to kVA: 520 ÷ 0.85 = about 612 kVA
Adds 20%: about 734 kVA
Chooses 750 kVA, with a reason
Calculates the current: about 902 A
Says what the current is used for, or checks with the designer

essays.stem: Describe the inspection and tests that are done on a new substation before it is energised, and who does them.
essays.modelAnswer: First the coordinator and the installer inspect the work against the drawings and specification: the equipment, the labels, the clearances, the tightness of connections, the cable glands and supports, the earthing and bonding, the oil level and the fence, locks and signs. Defects are recorded, fixed and checked again. Then the competent testing team does the tests, following the maker's instructions and the specification. These usually include insulation resistance tests on cables, transformer windings and switchgear; a turns ratio test on the transformer; oil tests on an oil-filled unit; earth resistance tests; checks of the CT connections and secondary injection tests on the protection relays; and checks that interlocks and earth switches work. All results are recorded on test sheets and compared with the required values. The government electrical inspector then inspects and approves the installation. Only after that do the authorised persons of the power company and the owner energise it, check the voltages and the phase rotation, and sign the energising record.
markingPoints: Visual inspection against drawings and specification, with defects fixed
Names several correct tests: insulation, ratio, oil, earth, protection
Tests done by a competent testing team and recorded
Inspection and approval before connection
Energising by authorised persons, with voltage and phase checks

essays.stem: Explain what documents should be handed over to the owner when a substation is completed, and why each one is needed.
essays.modelAnswer: The as-built drawings, including the single-line diagram and layout, show exactly what was installed and any changes, so future work is safe and correct. The test and commissioning records give the results of every test, which prove the work met the specification and give a baseline for later maintenance tests. The inspection and approval certificate shows the installation was accepted for connection. The makers' operation and maintenance manuals, data sheets and nameplate details tell the owner's staff how to operate and service the equipment and order spares. The protection settings record shows how each relay is set, so it can be checked or changed by competent people. The warranty documents protect the owner if equipment fails early. A spares list, the keys, the switching procedure and the operating labels are also handed over. I would check every document is complete, put them in an indexed file, and get the owner to sign that they have received them.
markingPoints: As-built drawings and why they matter
Test and commissioning records as proof and baseline
Inspection approval certificate
Maker's manuals, protection settings and warranties
Checks completeness and gets a signed receipt

practical1.title: Plan and programme the installation of a pad-mounted customer substation (desk exercise)
practical1.brief: This is a planning exercise done in the classroom. Nobody enters a substation. The assessor gives your group a project pack for a hotel substation: a single-line diagram, a site plan, extracts from the specification, an equipment list with delivery lead times, and the power company's requirements. As a group, prepare a coordination pack. Share the roles: one member writes the task list and draws the programme as a Gantt chart, marking the critical path; one makes a responsibility table showing who does each task and each interface (owner, designer, power company, civil contractor, crane company, jointers, testing team, inspector); one checks the equipment list against the single-line diagram and specification and writes a materials and equipment schedule with any queries; one writes an outline lifting plan for the transformer from the data given; and one writes a risk assessment for the project, including the controls near live plant. The group then holds a ten-minute 'coordination meeting' in which each member presents their part and the group agrees actions, which are minuted. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Project pack: single-line diagram, site plan, specification extracts, equipment list and lead times (supplied by the assessor)
Power company requirements sheet (supplied by the assessor)
Graph paper or a spreadsheet for the Gantt chart
Blank responsibility table, lifting plan, risk assessment and minutes forms
Calculators, rulers, coloured markers and flip-chart paper
photos: The Gantt chart with the critical path marked
The materials and equipment schedule with the queries raised
The outline lifting plan and the risk assessment
The coordination meeting, with each member presenting
The signed meeting minutes and action list
checklist: Put the tasks in a logical, workable order with long-lead items ordered early
Gave each task and interface a clear owner
Checked equipment against the single-line diagram and specification and raised real queries
Included the key points of a lifting plan and risk assessment
Kept all live work with authorised persons in the plan
Presented their part clearly and answered questions
safety: This is a desk exercise: no member enters or works in any substation
Plans must keep switching, earthing and energising with authorised persons only
Use only the figures the assessor gives; do not guess clearances or ratings for a real site
Keep the classroom tidy and walkways clear

practical2.title: Set out a full-size substation layout and carry out a receiving inspection of apparatus
practical2.brief: Your group sets out, full size, the layout of a small pad-mounted substation on the Centre's yard or workshop floor, and inspects 'delivered' apparatus. Nothing is connected to any supply and no digging is done. The assessor gives a layout drawing with dimensions and clearances (given as data), and a delivery pack. Part A: using tape measures, chalk lines or marking tape and cones, set out the plinth, the bund, the fence line and gates (with their swing), the cable trench routes and duct entries, the earth grid ring and electrode positions, the access route for the delivery truck and the crane position, and the danger sign positions. Check the clearances against the drawing and record them. Part B: carry out a receiving inspection of the items the assessor provides (for example a small dry-type training transformer, a switch-fuse unit and a cable termination kit, all never connected to a supply, or photos and data sheets of real items with planted faults). Check each item against the purchase order and specification, look for damage, and complete a receiving log and a non-conformance report for any problem. Share the roles so every member measures and marks, and every member inspects at least one item and signs for it. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Layout drawing with dimensions and clearances (supplied by the assessor)
Tape measures (30 m and 5 m), chalk line or floor marking tape, cones and pegs
Purchase order, specification extract and delivery notes (supplied by the assessor)
Training items or photos and data sheets with planted faults (supplied by the assessor)
Receiving log, clearance record and non-conformance report forms
Clipboards, pens and a camera or phone
photos: The marked-out plinth, bund and fence line with the gates
The cable trench routes, duct entries and earth grid positions
A member checking a clearance with the tape against the drawing
The truck access route and crane position marked
Each item being checked against the purchase order
The completed receiving log and non-conformance report
checklist: Read the layout drawing correctly and measured accurately
Marked out every feature in the right place, within the tolerance the assessor gives
Checked and recorded the clearances against the drawing
Checked each item's nameplate and paperwork against the order and specification
Found the planted faults and recorded them clearly
Completed and signed their part of the log and report
Worked safely and helped others in the group
safety: Nothing is connected to any supply; only the instructor may energise anything at the Centre
No excavation: mark the ground only
Use correct manual handling for training items, with two people for anything heavy
Keep the yard area coned off from vehicles, and wear safety boots and a high-visibility vest outdoors
